idea-plugin.name: Env Var Missing Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Cross-checks every real environment-variable access in your open file (process.env.PORT, process.env["PORT"], os.environ["DEBUG"], os.environ.get("DEBUG"), os.getenv("TIMEOUT")) against your project's real .env/.env.example files, and warns on any variable that's used in code but never declared anywhere -- with a real quick-fix to add it.

Scope (v0.1, deliberate):

  • Scans the file currently open in the editor, not the whole project on every keystroke -- the real, common case (you just typed a new process.env.X reference and want to know right now if it's declared).
  • JavaScript/TypeScript and Python -- the two ecosystems where reading env vars by string key (process.env.X/os.environ[...]) is the dominant pattern. Java/Kotlin are out of v0.1: that ecosystem's dominant pattern is Spring's @Value/application.properties injection, not direct System.getenv calls, so this specific code↔.env cross-check pattern is comparatively far less common there.
  • A variable with an explicit default right in the code (process.env.PORT || 3000, os.environ.get("DEBUG", "false"), os.getenv("TIMEOUT", 30)) is flagged as a weaker warning, not a full warning -- the code still runs fine without it declared, so it's real but less urgent.

Quick-fix: "Add VARNAME to .env.example" appends VARNAME= to your project's real .env.example -- or creates one from scratch (with a header comment noting it was generated) if your project has none at all.

Complements Env Diff Companion (which compares two .env files against each other) -- this plugin compares your actual code against your .env files instead.

100% static text analysis of files already open in your project -- no network call, no external process spawned. A project with no .env* file at all is handled as an honest "everything referenced is unmatched" case, never a crash.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no popups.

localInspection.displayName: Env var used but not declared in .env
